parsed.modern: Neither do we suppose civil history and the principles of animals to be overlooked. Without being acquainted with these, how could not young or accurate knowledge of the laws and political institutions of his country be acquired by the young generation! History expects to warn observation the fortune and the actions of other human beings, and thus supplies in some measure the place of experience; it teaches prudence, and affords exercise to the moral sense.
